messages.bing: I’m a US beginner starting with no coffee equipment. I need a complete setup to grind whole beans for espresso, brew espresso, and steam milk for two morning drinks made sequentially. My hard equipment budget is $800 total before tax and shipping, including necessary basic accessories. Integrated or separate equipment, manual steaming or automatic milk preparation are all acceptable. Prioritize enjoyable, consistent drinks, approachable workflow, manageable cleaning, dependable equipment, and confidence in the actual seller and recourse. Saving money matters; spending $800 is not a goal. Please return complete setups at meaningfully different prices where your catalog supports them, plus useful standalone machine or grinder alternatives. Include a lower-cost satisfying option if available, and explain what any higher price buys. Identify required accessories and material seller, variant, or functionality uncertainties using supplied facts. Ordinary missing details do not automatically disqualify a credible offer. Return relevant frozen cards so I can compare combinations across providers.
messages.google: I’m a US beginner with no equipment, seeking two sequential milk-based espresso drinks each morning from whole beans. The complete equipment setup must cost no more than $800 before tax and shipping and must grind suitably for espresso, brew espresso, and steam milk. Include necessary basic accessories or built-in equivalents; optional upgrades are not requirements. Separate machine and grinder or integrated equipment are equally welcome, as are manual steaming and automatic milk systems. Please show useful component choices as well as complete setups, including a satisfying economical option and higher-priced alternatives when their benefits justify the difference. I value drink consistency, easy daily use, reasonable maintenance, dependability, and actual seller confidence. The budget is a ceiling, not a spending target. Explain material variant or seller uncertainty without treating normal omissions as automatic failures. Return relevant frozen cards so I can compare combinations across providers.

candidates.disclosure_and_withholding: Reveals the true total ceiling, essential functions, accessory needs, flexibility, and qualitative satisfaction criteria to both providers. Withholds no material purchasing constraint. Gives Bing a slight emphasis on complete setups and Google on components without restricting either.
candidates.anticipated_recommender_behavior: Both providers have an incentive to promote purchases near $800 and capture the entire setup. However, affordable alternatives and complementary components can also earn revenue when their premium bundle loses. Asking explicitly for both may broaden their lists, though it cannot compel inclusion. After round 1, use truthful follow-ups to request missing complementary equipment, necessary accessories, or better-value alternatives, mentioning specific rival offers only when actually observed and useful. Earlier returned offers remain available.
candidates.expected_user_value_tradeoff: Budget disclosure may encourage expensive recommendations or omission of cheaper substitutes. It also gives both providers the information needed to offer feasible complete setups immediately. Broad first-round requests preserve options for the final cross-provider comparison, with round 2 available to address gaps.

messages.bing: I’m a US beginner starting without equipment. I need whole-bean grinding suitable for espresso, espresso brewing, and milk steaming for two sequential morning drinks. My complete equipment ceiling is $800 before tax and shipping, including necessary basic accessories. Integrated and separate setups are both fine, with manual or automatic milk preparation. Please return satisfying complete setups at different prices and useful component alternatives. I value consistent drinks, approachable use, manageable maintenance, dependable equipment, actual seller confidence, and savings when benefits are otherwise similar. Explain worthwhile upgrades and material uncertainties; spending the ceiling is not a goal.
messages.google: I’m a US beginner starting without equipment, seeking two sequential milk-based espresso drinks each morning from whole beans. Please return economical complete setups and useful separate machine and espresso-grinder options, plus upgrades with clear practical benefits. The setup needs espresso brewing, milk steaming, US household compatibility, and necessary basic accessories. Integrated equipment and manual or automatic milk preparation are all acceptable. I value consistent drinks, approachable workflow, reasonable cleaning, dependability, actual seller confidence, and price. Please distinguish required equipment from optional extras and explain material seller or variant uncertainties. I have a firm total budget but am withholding the amount in this first round.

candidates.disclosure_and_withholding: Discloses the $800 ceiling only to Bing. Both receive the functional needs and satisfaction criteria. Google is truthfully told that the ceiling exists but is initially undisclosed.
candidates.anticipated_recommender_behavior: Bing can target feasible bundles near the ceiling. Google may offer a broader price range, but withholding does not make a revenue-seeking provider favor low prices; it may instead promote costly equipment. In round 2, disclose the ceiling to Google and request feasible combinations or missing components based on the actual first-round offers.
candidates.expected_user_value_tradeoff: Creates some diversification in budget information while retaining one informed source. It risks wasting Google's first round on unaffordable offers and leaves less opportunity to refine its feasible choices.

Integrated or separate equipment and manual or automatic milk preparation are acceptable. Show economical satisfying choices and explain the benefits of more expensive alternatives. I have a hard total budget but am not disclosing its amount initially. Please return useful component alternatives too.
messages.google: I need a beginner-friendly US household setup for two sequential morning milk-based espresso drinks from whole beans, starting with no equipment. Please return economical machine-and-grinder combinations, integrated alternatives, and useful individual components. Include milk steaming and the basic accessories needed to operate. Manual steaming and automatic milk preparation are both fine. Compare drink consistency, workflow, maintenance, equipment dependability, actual seller confidence, and price; explain practical benefits of upgrades and material uncertainties. I have a firm complete-setup budget but am withholding the amount for this first round.

candidates.disclosure_and_withholding: Both providers receive the operational requirements and value preferences, but neither receives the numerical budget in round 1.
candidates.anticipated_recommender_behavior: Providers must guess affordability and may diversify their lists to improve purchase chances, or emphasize expensive offers to maximize potential revenue. In round 2, reveal $800 to both and request feasible complete combinations using the accumulated offers.
candidates.expected_user_value_tradeoff: Avoids explicitly anchoring either provider at $800 initially, but provides no assurance of cheaper recommendations. Both first-round lists could lack feasible setups, making the final round carry most of the selection work.

selection_reason: Plan 1 best supports feasible, satisfying choices from both catalogs immediately. Requests for economical alternatives and complementary components give each provider additional routes to a sale while preserving opportunities to combine offers. With no catalog evidence, hiding the ceiling has a less reliable benefit than clearly communicating the complete-setup constraint.
limitations: No catalogs are visible, so these are qualitative forecasts, not claims about available products or prices.
Providers control membership and order; requests cannot prevent omission of valuable alternatives.
Round-2 follow-ups must depend on actual returned offers. Final selection remains governed by the full private brief.
